'''Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Limited''' is an Indian multinational [[pharmaceutical]] company headquartered in [[Mumbai]].

== History ==
Glenmark Pharmaceuticals was founded in 1977 by [[Gracias Saldanha]] as a [[generic drug]] and [[Active ingredient|active pharmaceutical ingredient]] manufacturer. He named the company after his two sons. The company initially sold its products in India, Russia, and Africa. The company went public in India in 1999. Saldanha's son Glenn took over as CEO in 2001,<ref name=Emerging>{{Cite web |date=2007-10-27 |title=Emerging Company of the Year : Glenmark Pharmaceuticals |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/emerging-company-of-the-year-glenmark-pharmaceuticals/articleshow/2431780.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-08-03 |website=The Economic Times}}</ref> having returned to India after working at [[PricewaterhouseCoopers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-10-27 |title=Emerging Company of the Year : Glenmark Pharmaceuticals |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/emerging-company-of-the-year-glenmark-pharmaceuticals/articleshow/2431780.cms?from=mdr |website=The Economic Times}}</ref> In 2008 Glenmark was the fifth-biggest pharmaceutical company in India.<ref name="Hiscock">{{cite book|last1=Hiscock|first1=Geoff|title=India's Global Wealth Club: The Stunning Rise of Its Billionaires and Their Secrets of Success|date=2008|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=9780470822388|pages=65–66|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YiLBD_IpgIkC&pg=PA65|language=en}}</ref>

By 2011 the founder of the company was one of the richest men in India,<ref>{{cite web|title=India's Richest: #69 Gracias Saldanha|url=https://www.forbes.com/lists/2011/77/india-billionaires-11_Gracias-Saldanha_8GY4.html|work=Forbes|language=en|date=2011}}</ref> and Glenmark had worldwide sales of $778 million, a 37% increase over the last year's sales; the growth was driven by Glenmark's entry into the US and European generics markets.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Levin|first1=Jennifer|title=5. Glenmark Pharmaceuticals|url=http://www.fiercepharma.com/special-report/5-glenmark-pharmaceuticals|work=FiercePharma|language=en}}</ref>

In the mid-2010s the generics industry in general began transitioning to the end of an era of giant [[patent cliff]]s in the pharmaceutical industry; patented drugs with sales of around $28 billion were set to come off patent in 2018, but in 2019 only about $10 billion in revenue was set to open for competition, and less the next year. Companies in the industry responded with [[Consolidation (business)|consolidation]] or trying to generate new, patented drugs.<ref name=LiveMint2017>{{cite news|last1=Altstedter|first1=Ari|title=Glenmark's Glenn Saldanha seeks a new holy grail as generic drugs run dry|url=http://www.livemint.com/Companies/RAou6M0VoQyMHz9l2A5zYM/Glenmarks-Glenn-Saldanha-seeks-a-new-holy-grail-as-generic.html|work=Live Mint|date=18 May 2017}}</ref>

Under Glenn Saldanha, the company focused on developing new drugs<ref>{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=11 July 2019 |title=Glenmark, Torrent Pharma ink pact to co-market diabetes drug in India |work=Business Today |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/current/corporate/glenmark-torrent-pharma-ink-pact-to-comarket-diabetes-drug-in-india/story/363461.html |access-date=20 July 2019}}</ref><ref name=LiveMint2017/> and [[biosimilar]]s in the fields of cancer, dermatology and respiratory diseases, which it sought to monetize by partnering with major pharmaceutical companies.<ref name=LiveMint2017/><ref name=LiveMint2016>{{cite news|last1=Trivedi|first1=Isha|title=We plan to out-license our entire novel drugs pipeline: Glenmark CMD|url=http://www.livemint.com/Companies/fZfCaiKR2hDJjaCEcXSuGL/We-plan-to-outlicense-our-entire-novel-drugs-pipeline-Glen.html|work=Live Mint|date=22 December 2016}}</ref> In 2016 it had four such drugs in clinical trials.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Altstedter|first1=Ari|title=Glenmark Expects Cash Surge From License Deals in Next 18 Months|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-07-15/glenmark-expects-cash-surge-from-license-deals-in-next-18-months|work=Bloomberg.com|date=15 July 2016}}</ref> Its R&D developed a drug to treat [[asthma]] and [[Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease|COPD]] and licensed this to [[North America]] and [[Japan]]. It also licensed out a new [[diabetes]] drug to the German [[Merck Group|Merck]].<ref name="Emerging" />{{Unreliable medical source|date=June 2025}} For the financial year 2016–2017 its sales were around 81 billion INR (ca. $1.25 billion), making it the fourth-biggest Indian pharmaceutical company.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Seo |first1=Don |date=30 July 2024 |title=India Pharmaceutical Sector – Small Growth in Sales during FY 2016-17 |url=https://kabarluwuraya.com/india-pharmaceutical-sector-small-growth-in-sales-during-fy-2016-17/ |work=KabarLuwuRaya |language=en}}</ref>

In May 2019, Yasir Rawjee became CEO of Glenmark Life Sciences.<ref>{{cite news |title=Glenmark appoints Yasir Rawjee as CEO of Glenmark Life Sciences |url=https://business.medicaldialogues.in/glenmark-appoints-yasir-rawjee-ceo-glenmark-life-sciences/ |work=Medical Dialogues |date=8 May 2019}}</ref>

In March 2020, Glenmark Pharmaceuticals sold intimate hygiene brand, VWash, to [[Hindustan Unilever]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dsouza |first=Sharleen |date= |title=HUL To Acquire VWash From Glenmark Pharma |url=https://www.ndtvprofit.com/business/hul-to-acquire-vwash-from-glenmark-pharma-10261203 |url-status=live |access-date= |work=[[NDTV]]}}</ref>

In 2024, Glenmark completed the sale of its 75% stake in Glenmark Life Sciences (GLS) to [[Nirma]] for approximately ₹5,651 crore (US$680 million).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Livemint |date=2024-07-10 |title=Stake sale: Glenmark Pharma to offload 7.84% stake in Glenmark Life Science through OFS {{!}} Company Business News |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/stake-sale-glenmark-pharma-to-offload-7-84-stake-in-glenmark-life-science-through-ofs-11720614083369.html |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref>

In August 2025, Glenmark Pharmaceuticals transferred its consumer care business into a new wholly owned subsidiary named Glenmark Consumer Care Limited.<ref>{{Cite news| date=2025-09-15 |title=Glenmark Pharma to transfer its consumer care biz to Glenmark Consumer Care |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/glenmark-pharma-to-transfer-its-consumer-care-biz-to-glenmark-consumer-care-125091501117_1.html |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=Business Standard |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=www.ETPharma.com |title=Glenmark to hive-off consumer care biz into new subsidiary |url=https://pharma.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/pharma-industry/glenmark-pharmaceuticals-splits-consumer-care-business-into-new-subsidiary/123346925 |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=ETPharma.com |language=en}}</ref>

== R&D and Partnerships ==

=== Formation of Ichnos Glenmark Innovation (IGI) ===
In January 2024, Glenmark and its subsidiary Ichnos Sciences formed ''Ichnos Glenmark Innovation (IGI)'' to combine small‑molecule and [[biologics]] R&D for oncology, with three molecules already in clinical trials and two holding U.S. FDA orphan drug designations.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pilla |first=Viswanath |date=2024-01-30 |title=Glenmark forms alliance with Ichnos to develop anti-cancer drugs |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/pharmaceuticals/glenmark-ichnos-sciences-form-alliance-for-new-drug-discovery-in-cancer-treatment/articleshow/107266350.cms |access-date=2026-03-06 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

=== Global Licensing Agreement with AbbVie ===
In July 2025, Ichnos Glenmark Innovation (IGI), a wholly owned subsidiary of Glenmark Pharmaceuticals,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-10 |title=Glenmark Pharma's innovation arm signs exclusive licensing agreement with AbbVie for ISB 2001 - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/glenmark-pharma-share-price-exclusive-licensing-agrement-igi-abbvie-isb-2001-impact-outlook-19635203.htm |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=CNBCTV18 |language=en}}</ref> entered into a global licensing agreement with US-based biopharmaceutical company [[AbbVie]] for the development and commercialization of '''ISB 2001'''. ISB 2001 is a first-in-class trispecific antibody developed using IGI's proprietary BEAT platform, currently in Phase 1 clinical trials for the treatment of relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Conroy |first=Russ |date=2026-02-14 |title=FDA Gives Fast-Track Designation to ISB 2001 in Relapsed/Refractory Myeloma {{!}} CancerNetwork |url=https://www.cancernetwork.com/view/fda-gives-fast-track-designation-to-isb-2001-in-relapsed-refractory-myeloma |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=www.cancernetwork.com |language=en}}</ref> Under the terms of the agreement, AbbVie secured exclusive rights to develop, manufacture, and commercialize the drug in North America, Europe, Japan, and Greater China, while Glenmark retained rights for India and other emerging markets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Glenmark arm IGI licenses cancer drug to AbbVie for upfront $700 mn with $1.22 bn in milestone payment |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/glenmark-pharma-s-arm-us-company-abbvie-sign-licensing-agreement-for-cancer-drug-13260122.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250711180227/https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/glenmark-pharma-s-arm-us-company-abbvie-sign-licensing-agreement-for-cancer-drug-13260122.html |archive-date=2025-07-11 |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en-US}}</ref> The deal included an upfront payment of $700 million to IGI, with potential milestone payments totaling up to $1.225 billion, alongside tiered double-digit royalties on future net sales.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chennamkulath |first=Unni K. |date=2025-07-11 |title=Glenmark-AbbVie deal: A turning point in Indian drug innovation |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/business/2025/Jul/11/glenmark-abbvie-deal-a-turning-point-in-indian-drug-innovation |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

=== Partnership with Hengrui Pharma and Hansoh Pharma ===
In September 2025 licensed [[Jiangsu Hengrui|Hengrui’s]] trastuzumab rezetecan (SHR‑A1811), a [[HER2]]‑targeted ADC, for selected markets, with milestone‑linked economics disclosed in media reports.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Glenmark Pharma signs $18 mn deal with Hengrui for cancer therapy drug |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/glenmark-pharma-hengrui-18mn-deal-trastuzumab-rezetecan-cancer-drug-125092401349_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925154057/https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/glenmark-pharma-hengrui-18mn-deal-trastuzumab-rezetecan-cancer-drug-125092401349_1.html |archive-date=2025-09-25 |access-date=2026-03-06 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Liu |first=Angus |date=2025-09-24 |title=Glenmark, Hengrui ink $1.1B deal for HER2 ADC |url=https://www.fiercepharma.com/pharma/potential-11b-deal-glenmark-grabs-certain-rights-hengrui-adc-rival-enhertu |access-date=2026-03-06 |website=www.fiercepharma.com |language=en}}</ref>

In December 2025, Glenmark Specialty S.A. in‑licensed [[aumolertinib]] (third‑generation [[EGFR inhibitors|EGFR‑TKI]]) from [[Hansoh Pharmaceutical|Hansoh Pharma]] for multi‑regional rights - adding an MHRA/NMPA‑approved lung cancer therapy to its pipeline.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Glenmark enters collaboration and distribution agreement with Jiangsu Hansoh Pharma for Aumolertinib, a third-generation GFR-TKI to treat NSCLC |url=https://www.pharmabiz.com/NewsDetails.aspx?aid=183084&sid=2 |access-date=2026-03-06 |website=www.pharmabiz.com}}</ref> 

== Products & Services ==

=== Telma (Telmisartan) ===
Glenmark launched its [[telmisartan]] brand, ''Telma'', in 2003 for the treatment of hypertension and cardiovascular indications.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2025-02-15 |title=Glenmark Telma’s journey to Rs 1000cr becomes a Harvard case study |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/healthcare-the-rise-of-glenmarks-telma-how-this-blood-pressure-drug-became-a-rs-1000-crore-brand-3750269/ |access-date=2026-03-14 |website=The Financial Express |language=en}}</ref> By 2024, the Telma brand family, including 16 line extensions, reached an annual turnover of ₹1,036 crore. The brand's market entry and growth strategy were the subject of a 2015 case study by '''[[Harvard Business Publishing|Harvard Business Publishing Education]]''', which examined its competition with the then-market-dominant molecule, [[Ramipril]].<ref name=":2" />

=== GlipiQ launch ===
Following approval from the '''[[Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation|Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO)]]''', Glenmark Pharmaceuticals launched '''Glipiq'''<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kumar |first=N. Ravi |date=2026-03-21 |title=Sun Pharma, Dr. Reddy’s, Zydus, Glenmark roll out generic Semaglutide |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/sun-pharma-dr-reddys-zydus-glenmark-roll-out-generic-semaglutide/article70768590.ece |access-date=2026-03-28 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>, a biosimilar version of the [[GLP-1 receptor agonist]] '''[[semaglutide]]'''. The medication is indicated for the treatment of [[type 2 diabetes]] and represents part of the company's expansion into the metabolic health and weight-management segment in India.<ref>{{Cite web |title=India’s GLP‑1 moment is here—the weight‑loss drug wars begin |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/news/indias-glp%E2%80%911-moment-is-here-the-weight%E2%80%91loss-drug-wars-begin/2992364/1 |access-date=2026-03-28 |website=www.forbesindia.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Glenmark Pharma launches GLIPIQ (semaglutide) in India for Type 2 Diabetes at lower cost |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/glenmark-pharma-launches-glipiq-semaglutide-in-india-for-type-2-diabetes-at-lower-cost-126032100423_1.html |access-date=2026-03-28 |work=[[Business Standard]]}}</ref>

== Quality control issues ==
In October 2019, following an inspection by the [[Food and Drug Administration|US Food and Drug Administration]] (FDA) of Glenmark's plant in [[Himachal Pradesh]], the FDA sent Glenmark a [[FDA warning letter|warning letter]] in which it detailed "significant violations of current good manufacturing practice."<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Callahan |first=Patricia |last2=Cenziper |first2=Debbie |last3=Rose |first3=Megan |date=2024-12-12 |title=The FDA Hasn’t Inspected This Drug Factory After 7 Recalls for the Same Flaw, 1 Potentially Deadly |url=https://www.propublica.org/article/glenmark-pharmaceuticals-recalls-fda-oversight |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250715014242/https://www.propublica.org/article/glenmark-pharmaceuticals-recalls-fda-oversight |archive-date=2025-07-15 |access-date=2025-07-30 |website=[[ProPublica]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Godwin |first=Francis |date=2019-10-03 |title=Warning Letter - Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Limited - MARCS-CMS 582701 |url=https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/glenmark-pharmaceuticals-limited-582701-10032019 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250418061643/https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/glenmark-pharmaceuticals-limited-582701-10032019 |archive-date=2025-04-18 |access-date=2025-07-30 |website=[[Food and Drug Administration]] |language=en}}</ref>

In August 2021, Glenmark recalled every product being produced at its plant near [[Charlotte, North Carolina]].<ref name=":1" /> A subsequent investigation in 2022 by the FDA documented 17 violations of manufacturing standards and resulted in an FDA warning letter for the plant.<ref name=":1" />

In November 2022, the FDA sent Glenmark a warning letter about its plant in [[Goa|Goa, India]], which stated that the plant lacked the procedures necessary to verify that drugs produced by the plant had the strength, quality, and purity claimed by Glenmark.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Godwin |first=Francis |date=2022-11-22 |title=Warning Letter - Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Limited - MARCS-CMS 637314 |url=https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/glenmark-pharmaceuticals-limited-637314-11222022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250518184939/https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/glenmark-pharmaceuticals-limited-637314-11222022 |archive-date=2025-05-18 |access-date=2025-07-30 |website=[[Food and Drug Administration]] |language=en}}</ref>

In September 2024, Glenmark's product Telma-H ([[telmisartan]]) was subject to a ‘Not of Standard Quality’ (NSQ) alert by India's [[Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation]] (CDSCO).<ref name="BajeliDatt2024">{{Cite web |last=Bajeli-Datt |first=Kavita |date=2024-09-25 |title=Antacid Pan D, Paracetamol, Glimepiride among over 50 drugs that fail quality test |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/2024/Sep/25/antacid-pan-d-paracetamol-glimepiride-among-over-50-drugs-fail-quality-test |access-date=2024-10-05 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}}</ref> The company asserted that they had not produced the drug.<ref name="BajeliDatt2024" />

In July 2025, the FDA sent Glenmark another warning letter, following an inspection of the company's plant in [[Madhya Pradesh]] in February 2025 that uncovered problems with cleaning and drug testing at the plant.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Callahan |first=Patricia |date=2025-03-20 |title=The FDA Finally Visited an Indian Drug Factory Linked to U.S. Deaths. It Found Problems. |url=https://www.propublica.org/article/glenmark-pharmaceuticals-recalls-fda-inspection |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250723042833/https://www.propublica.org/article/glenmark-pharmaceuticals-recalls-fda-inspection |archive-date=2025-07-23 |access-date=2025-07-30 |website=[[ProPublica]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Callahan |first=Patricia |date=2025-07-28 |title=The FDA Is Cracking Down on an Indian Drugmaker Investigated by ProPublica Last Year |url=https://www.propublica.org/article/fda-letter-glenmark-pharmaceuticals |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250729104157/https://www.propublica.org/article/fda-letter-glenmark-pharmaceuticals |archive-date=2025-07-29 |access-date=2025-07-30 |website=[[ProPublica]] |language=en}}</ref> In the letter, the FDA noted that similar problems had been found at three other Glenmark manufacturing sites that had previously been the subject of warning letters, stating that "These repeated failures at multiple sites demonstrate that management oversight and control over the manufacture of drugs is inadequate."<ref name=":0" />
